Cross-wavelet coherence analysis

Source: R/analyse_wavelet_coherence.R, R/zzz_aliases_american.R
analyse_wavelet_coherence.Rd

Computes the cross-wavelet transform and wavelet coherence between two time/depth series using a superlet-based wavelet approach. The function internally interpolates both input series onto a common grid, computes individual wavelet transforms, and derives cross-wavelet power, phase, and coherence with configurable smoothing.

Usage

analyse_wavelet_coherence(
  data_1,
  data_2,
  dj = 1/100,
  lowerPeriod = 2,
  upperPeriod = 1024,
  verbose = FALSE,
  omega_nr = 8,
  wavelet = "morlet",
  wavelet_order = NULL,
  n_simulations = 10,
  window.type.t = 4,
  window.type.s = 4,
  abs_window_t = 500,
  abs_window_s = 0.5
)

analyze_wavelet_coherence(
  data_1,
  data_2,
  dj = 1/100,
  lowerPeriod = 2,
  upperPeriod = 1024,
  verbose = FALSE,
  omega_nr = 8,
  wavelet = "morlet",
  wavelet_order = NULL,
  n_simulations = 10,
  window.type.t = 4,
  window.type.s = 4,
  abs_window_t = 500,
  abs_window_s = 0.5
)

Arguments

data_1

First record: a two-column matrix or data frame with depth/time in column 1 and the proxy value in column 2 (no NA values). Both records are sorted and linearly interpolated to a common, regular grid over their overlapping interval, with the coarser of the two median sampling intervals. Required, no default.

data_2

Second record, in the same format and depth/time unit as data_1 (two-column matrix or data frame: depth/time, proxy). The phase is the phase of data_1 minus that of data_2. Required, no default.

dj

Spacing between successive scales in octaves (numeric, > 0), passed to analyse_wavelet; dj=1/x gives x periods per doubling of the period, smaller values give a finer period axis. Default=1/100.

lowerPeriod

Shortest period to analyse, in the same unit as the depth/time column of the records (numeric, > 0; at least twice the common sampling interval). Default=2.

upperPeriod

Longest period to analyse, in the same unit as the depth/time column of the records (numeric, > lowerPeriod). Default=1024.

verbose

Print the sampling interval to which the records were interpolated, passed to analyse_wavelet (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

omega_nr

Number of cycles (central angular frequency omega_0) of the Morlet wavelet, passed to analyse_wavelet (numeric, > 0); controls the trade-off between period and depth/time resolution. Default=8.

wavelet

Mother wavelet (character string or function), passed to analyse_wavelet, given as a name (PyWavelets style names with the order appended, such as "db4", "sym8", "cgau3", "gaus2" or "cmor1.5-1", also work) or as a function psi_hat(omega) that returns the Fourier transform of a user defined mother wavelet. Analytic (complex) wavelets, which give phase and amplitude and can be synchrosqueezed: "morlet" (default; aliases "gabor", "amor"), "morlet0" (exactly zero mean Morlet, admissible for a small omega_nr; alias "morlex"), "paul" (alias "cauchy"), "morse" (generalised Morse wavelet of Olhede and Walden, 2002; aliases "gmw", "airy"), "bump", "cmor" (complex Morlet with bandwidth and centre frequency as in Matlab/PyWavelets), "cgau" (analytic Gaussian derivative; "cmhat" is the complex Mexican hat), "shannon" (complex Shannon, box spectrum), "fbsp" (frequency B-spline), "meyer", "loggabor" (alias "lognormal"), "gammatone" (asymmetric in time: sharp onset, slow decay) and "hann" (raised cosine band). Real wavelets, which give a real transform (no phase or envelope): "dog" (derivative of Gaussian; "mexh", "ricker", "marr" and "sombrero" are the Mexican hat, order 2), "morl" (real Morlet), "hhat" (Hermitian hat), "poisson", and the orthogonal wavelets "haar", "db" (Daubechies), "sym" (Symlets) and "battle" (Battle-Lemarie spline wavelets), which are computed in the frequency domain from their filters. The period axis of the orthogonal wavelets is approximate because their spectra are broad and not symmetric. A narrow wavelet (Paul, low-order DOG, Shannon, Haar) resolves position well, a wide one (Morse with a large beta, Morlet with a high omega_nr, bump) resolves period well. Default="morlet".

wavelet_order

Parameter(s) of the wavelet (numeric scalar or vector; NULL uses the defaults listed here): paul: order m (default 4); dog: derivative m (default 2); morse: c(gamma, beta) or beta alone with gamma = 3 (default c(3, 20)); bump: c(mu, sigma) (default c(5, 0.6)); cmor: c(bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(1.5, 1)); cgau: derivative m (default 4); shannon: c(bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(2, 1.5)); fbsp: c(m, bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(2, 2, 1.5)); loggabor: c(centre angular frequency, log-width) (default c(6, 0.25)); meyer and hhat have no parameter; morlet0: omega_0 (default omega_nr); morl: omega_0 (default 5); poisson: order n (default 2); gammatone: c(n, centre angular frequency, bandwidth) (default c(4, 6, 1.5)); hann: c(centre angular frequency, half width) (default c(6, 3)); db: number of vanishing moments 1 to 20 (default 4, "haar" = "db1"); sym: 2 to 20 (default 8); battle: spline order 1, 3, 5 or 7 (default 3). For the Morlet wavelet use omega_nr. Passed to analyse_wavelet. Default=NULL.

n_simulations

Number of simulations (integer). Not used: reserved for a future significance test. Default=10.

window.type.t

Type of the smoothing window applied in the depth/time direction before the coherence is computed, given as a number or a character code: 0 or "none" (no smoothing), 1 or "bar" (Bartlett), 2 or "tri" (triangular), 3 or "box" (boxcar), 4 or "han" (Hanning), 5 or "ham" (Hamming), 6 or "bla" (Blackman). Default=4 (Hanning).

window.type.s

Type of the smoothing window applied in the period (scale) direction; same options as window.type.t. Default=4 (Hanning).

abs_window_t

Length of the smoothing window in the depth/time direction, in the same unit as the depth/time column of the records (numeric, > 0); converted to an odd number of samples and capped at about a quarter of the record length (with a warning). Longer windows give smoother but less local coherence. Default=500.

abs_window_s

Length of the smoothing window in the period (scale) direction, in octaves (numeric, > 0; converted to an odd number of scale steps of size dj). Default=0.5.

Value

A list of class containing: Wave Smoothed cross-wavelet transform (complex) Coherence Wavelet coherence matrix Phase Phase difference between the two signals Coh.avg Average coherence over time Period (m)vector corresponding to scales Scale Wavelet scales dt Time step of interpolated grid dj Scale resolution axis.1 Time/depth axis axis.2 Period axis nc, nr Dimensions of the wavelet matrices x1, y1 Interpolated first dataset x2, y2 Interpolated second dataset

References

Torrence, C., and G. P. Compo (1998). A practical guide to wavelet analysis. Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society, 79(1), 61–78.

Author

plotting code based on the "analyze.coherency" function of the 'WaveletComp' R package

Examples

# \donttest{
# Generate two synthetic signals
t <- seq(0, 1000, by = 1)
x1 <- sin(2 * pi * t / 100) + rnorm(length(t), 0, 0.5)
x2 <- sin(2 * pi * t / 100 + pi/4) + rnorm(length(t), 0, 0.5)

data_1 <- cbind(t, x1)
data_2 <- cbind(t, x2)

coh <- analyse_wavelet_coherence(
  data_1 = data_1,
  data_2 = data_2,
  lowerPeriod = 2,
  upperPeriod = 256
)

# }
